newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index falls in listless trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index falls in listless trading.

text.p: The Slovak SAX index eased in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with brokers saying the bourse remains paralysed by a liquidity squeeze on the interbank money market.
"I don't expect this situation to improve unless some liquidity appears in the system," Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt Securities said.
Although the central bank added a small amount of liquidity to the interbank market on Wednesday, the market was still very short with overnight rates over 50 percent.
Krutil added that the current changes to the SAX index were probably unrepresentative of any underlying changes as volumes of shares traded on the BSE remained very low.
Only 675 shares were traded on the BSE's listed floor, with turnover at just 572,440 crowns. The overall figures were boosted by direct trades.
Steel maker VSZ dominated what trading there was, with 425 shares matched at an unchanged price of 700 crowns.
Overall volume, including direct deals, increased to 247,161 shares from 228,523 on Tuesday. Turnover rose to 178.6 million crowns from 57.43 million.
